breakfast.name: Syrnyky (Curd Pancakes)
instructions: Mix curd with egg, flour, sugar
Shape into patties
Fry in butter until golden
Serve with sour cream and jam
breakfast.description: Sweet curd cheese pancakes — a Ukrainian morning tradition.

imageCredit.author: Tatyana Morozyuk, color processing by Off-shell

breakfast.name: Deruny (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Grate potatoes and onion, squeeze dry
Mix with egg and flour
Fry until crispy
Serve with sour cream

breakfast.name: Syrniki (Cottage Cheese Pancakes)
instructions: Syrniki are Ukrainian (and broader Eastern European) cottage cheese pancakes
Tvorog (farmer's cheese) mixed with egg, flour, and sugar into small patties
Pan-fried in butter until golden on both sides
Served with sour cream (smetana) and jam or fresh berries
A beloved breakfast -- quick to make and deeply comforting
The tvorog must be pressed dry or the syrniki fall apart
breakfast.description: Ukrainian cottage cheese pancakes -- syrniki, farmer's cheese (tvorog) mixed with egg and flour, pan-fried in butter until golden. Served with sour cream and jam. The tvorog must be pressed dry or they fall apart. Quick, comforting breakfast.

imageCredit.author: Tatyana Morozyuk, color processing by Off-shell

breakfast.name: Mlyntsi (Ukrainian Crepes)
ingredients: Filling: tvorog and raisins, or meat, or mushrooms
instructions: Mlyntsi (also called nalisniki when filled) are Ukrainian crepes
Thin, delicate crepes cooked on a hot pan
Filled with sweetened tvorog and raisins (sweet version) or ground meat (savory)
Rolled up and sometimes pan-fried again for crispiness
Part of the Eastern Slavic crepe tradition (blini/nalisniki/mlyntsi)
Eaten at breakfast, as a snack, or for Maslenitsa (Butter Week before Lent)
breakfast.description: Ukrainian crepes -- mlyntsi, thin crepes filled with sweetened tvorog and raisins (sweet) or ground meat (savory), rolled and pan-fried again. Part of the Eastern Slavic crepe tradition. Eaten at breakfast and during Maslenitsa (Butter Week).

lunch.name: Borscht
instructions: Cook meat broth
Add potatoes, cook 10 min
Sauté grated beets with tomato paste
Add cabbage, beets, carrots, onion to broth
Simmer 20 min
Serve with sour cream, dill, and bread
lunch.description: Ukraine's national dish — beet soup with sour cream and pampushky.

lunch.name: Varenyky (Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: potato and onion, cherry, or cottage cheese
instructions: Make dough, roll thin
Cut circles, fill
Pinch closed, boil until they float
Toss with butter
Serve with sour cream and dill

lunch.name: Varenyky (Ukrainian Dumplings)
ingredients: Filling: mashed potato and farmer's cheese, or sauerkraut, or cherries (sweet)
Sour cream (smetana) and fried onions (for serving)
instructions: Varenyky are the Ukrainian dumplings -- the national comfort food
Thin dough wrapped around a filling and boiled
The most classic filling: mashed potato mixed with farmer's cheese
Sauerkraut filling for a sour, tangy version
Cherry filling for sweet varenyky -- a summer treat
Served with sour cream and crispy fried onions
Every Ukrainian grandmother has her own varenyky recipe and technique
Varenyky are the Ukrainian identity food -- festivals, holidays, everyday meals
Similar to Polish pierogi but the name and some fillings differ
lunch.description: Ukrainian national dumplings -- varenyky, thin dough around potato-cheese, sauerkraut, or cherry filling, boiled and served with sour cream and fried onions. Every grandmother has her own recipe. The Ukrainian identity food: festivals, holidays, everyday. Similar to pierogi.

lunch.name: Holubtsi (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
ingredients: Filling: rice and ground pork/beef, onion, garlic
instructions: Holubtsi are Ukrainian stuffed cabbage rolls -- a dish found across Eastern Europe
Cabbage leaves blanched, filled with seasoned meat and rice, rolled tight
Baked in tomato sauce until the cabbage is tender
Served with sour cream
A dish for Christmas Eve (Sviata Vecheria) -- the meatless version uses mushroom filling
The name comes from "holub" (dove) -- the rolls are shaped like small doves
A labor of love -- making holubtsi takes patience and skill in rolling
lunch.description: Ukrainian stuffed cabbage rolls -- holubtsi (from holub, dove -- shaped like small doves), cabbage leaves filled with seasoned meat and rice, baked in tomato sauce. Served with sour cream. A Christmas Eve dish (meatless mushroom version). A labor of love in rolling.

lunch.name: Solyanka (Sour and Salty Soup)
ingredients: Lemon slice and sour cream (for serving)
instructions: Solyanka is the Ukrainian/Russian sour and salty soup
A rich, complex soup with multiple smoked meats and pickled ingredients
The sourness comes from pickled cucumbers, olives, and lemon
The saltiness from smoked meats and capers
Served with a lemon slice in the bowl and a spoonful of sour cream
A hangover cure -- the richness and sourness are restorative
lunch.description: Ukrainian sour-salty soup -- solyanka, multiple smoked meats simmered with pickled cucumbers, olives, capers, and tomato paste. Served with a lemon slice and sour cream. Rich and complex. A famous hangover cure.

dinner.name: Chicken Kyiv
instructions: Pound chicken, place herb butter inside
Roll chicken around butter, secure
Coat in flour, egg, breadcrumbs
Deep fry until golden
Rest 5 min — butter should gush when cut
dinner.description: The legendary butter-stuffed breaded chicken breast.

dinner.name: Holubtsi (Cabbage Rolls)
instructions: Blanch cabbage leaves
Mix filling
Roll cabbage around filling
Pack in pot with tomato sauce
Bake or simmer 60 min
Serve with sour cream
dinner.description: Cabbage rolls filled with pork and rice.

dinner.name: Chicken Kyiv
ingredients: Butter (cold, seasoned with garlic, dill, parsley)
instructions: Chicken Kyiv is the butter-stuffed breaded chicken -- a dish famous worldwide
A cold herb butter is placed inside a pounded chicken breast
The chicken is rolled around the butter, breaded, and fried
When cut open: a burst of melted herb butter flows out -- the spectacle
The origin is debated -- likely French-influenced (Kiev/Kyiv was very francophile)
Named after the Ukrainian capital
The key: the butter must be very cold before wrapping, and the seal must be tight
dinner.description: Famous butter-stuffed chicken -- Chicken Kyiv, cold herb butter (garlic, dill, parsley) sealed inside a pounded breast, breaded, and fried. When cut: melted butter bursts out. Named after the Ukrainian capital. French-influenced technique. The seal must be tight.

dinner.name: Deruny (Potato Pancakes)
instructions: Deruny are Ukrainian potato pancakes -- crispy, golden, and comforting
Raw potatoes grated and mixed with onion, egg, and a little flour
Pan-fried in oil until crispy on both sides
Served with sour cream
Similar to latkes (Jewish), Kartoffelpuffer (German), draniki (Belarusian)
A dish of the potato belt -- Ukraine is one of the world's largest potato producers
Quick, cheap, and satisfying -- peasant food elevated to comfort classic
dinner.description: Ukrainian potato pancakes -- deruny, raw grated potato and onion fried until crispy golden. Served with sour cream. Part of the Eastern European potato pancake family (latkes, draniki). Ukraine is one of the world's largest potato producers. Peasant food elevated to comfort classic.

dinner.name: Pampushky (Garlic Bread Rolls)
ingredients: Flour, yeast, milk, egg, butter, sugar, salt
Garlic sauce: garlic crushed with oil, dill, and salt
instructions: Pampushky are Ukrainian soft garlic bread rolls -- the essential accompaniment to borscht
A soft, slightly sweet yeast dough baked into small round rolls
While hot from the oven, drenched in a garlic-dill-oil sauce
The garlic soaks into the warm bread
Borscht without pampushky is considered incomplete
The combination of beet soup and garlic bread is the Ukrainian comfort meal
dinner.description: Ukrainian soft garlic bread rolls -- pampushky, yeast dough baked into small rounds and drenched in garlic-dill-oil sauce while hot. The essential accompaniment to borscht. Borscht without pampushky is considered incomplete.

snacks.name: Pampushky (Garlic Bread)
ingredients: Dough: flour, yeast, water, sugar, salt
Garlic sauce: garlic, dill, oil, salt
instructions: Make yeast dough, rise
Shape into small buns
Bake at 200°C 15 min
Toss hot buns in garlic-dill sauce
snacks.description: Soft garlic buns — the essential borscht companion.

snacks.name: Salo (Cured Pork Fat)
ingredients: Pork fatback (with or without a thin meat layer)
instructions: Salo is the Ukrainian national delicacy -- cured pork fat
Pork fatback cured in salt and garlic for several days
Sliced thin and eaten on dark rye bread (chornyi khlib) with garlic
Sometimes smoked for extra flavor
Salo is a cultural icon -- there are festivals, songs, and jokes about salo
It is the most emblematic Ukrainian food -- more than even borscht
Eaten as a snack, appetizer, or with vodka (horilka)
snacks.description: Ukrainian cultural icon -- salo, cured pork fatback with salt and garlic, sliced thin on dark rye bread. More emblematic than borscht. There are festivals, songs, and jokes about salo. Eaten as a snack or with horilka (Ukrainian vodka).

snacks.name: Pirozhki (Fried Stuffed Buns)
ingredients: Filling: mashed potato, or cabbage, or meat
instructions: Pirozhki are small fried stuffed buns -- a street food across Ukraine and Russia
Soft yeast dough filled with potato, cabbage, or seasoned meat
Fried until golden brown
Sold by babushkas at train stations and markets
Eaten on the go -- the portable meal
snacks.description: Ukrainian fried stuffed buns -- pirozhki, soft yeast dough with potato, cabbage, or meat filling, fried golden. Sold by babushkas at train stations and markets. The portable meal.

snacks.name: Kvasheni Ohirky (Pickled Cucumbers)
instructions: Ukrainian pickled cucumbers are naturally fermented -- no vinegar
Cucumbers brined in salt water with garlic, dill, and leaves
The cherry and horseradish leaves keep the cucumbers crunchy
Fermented for several days to weeks
A staple of the Ukrainian table -- served alongside every meal
Essential with salo, borscht, and horilka
snacks.description: Ukrainian naturally fermented pickles -- kvasheni ohirky, cucumbers brined with garlic, dill, cherry leaves, and horseradish leaves (for crunch). No vinegar -- pure lactic fermentation. Served alongside every meal. Essential with salo and borscht.

desserts.name: Medovik (Honey Cake)
instructions: Make honey dough, roll thin layers
Bake each layer
Stack with sour cream filling between
Refrigerate overnight to soften
desserts.description: Multi-layered honey cake with sour cream — worth the wait.

desserts.name: Medovik (Honey Cake)
ingredients: Sour cream filling (sweetened sour cream between layers)
instructions: Medovik is the Ukrainian and Russian honey cake -- many thin layers with cream
Multiple thin honey-flavored cake layers baked one at a time
Stacked with sweetened sour cream between each layer
Refrigerated overnight -- the cream softens the layers into a tender, melting cake
The overnight rest is essential -- fresh medovik is not medovik
A celebration cake -- birthdays, holidays
The labor of baking each layer individually makes it a labor of love
desserts.description: Ukrainian many-layered honey cake -- medovik, thin honey-flavored cake layers stacked with sweetened sour cream, refrigerated overnight until the layers melt together. The overnight rest is essential. A labor of love -- each layer baked individually. Celebration cake.

desserts.name: Paska (Easter Bread)
ingredients: Flour, yeast, eggs (many), butter, sugar, milk
instructions: Paska is the Ukrainian Easter bread -- tall, domed, and richly decorated
An enriched yeast dough with many eggs and butter -- like a brioche
Studded with raisins and candied peel
Baked in tall cylindrical molds -- the dome rises above the rim
Topped with white icing and colorful sprinkles
Taken to church on Easter morning to be blessed by the priest
Part of the Easter basket (paskhalny koshyk) alongside eggs and salo
Baking paska is an Easter tradition -- the dough must be treated gently (no loud noises while it rises)
desserts.description: Ukrainian Easter bread -- paska, tall domed enriched bread with eggs, butter, raisins, topped with white icing and sprinkles. Taken to church on Easter morning to be blessed. Part of the Easter basket alongside eggs and salo. The dough must rise in silence.

drinks.name: Uzvar (Dried Fruit Compote)
instructions: Simmer dried fruits 15 min
Cool, serve cold with fruit

drinks.name: Horilka (Vodka)
instructions: Distill grain or potato mash
Often infused with honey and chili (pertsivka)

drinks.name: Uzvar (Dried Fruit Compote)
ingredients: Dried fruits: apples, pears, prunes, cherries
instructions: Uzvar is the Ukrainian dried fruit compote -- a traditional Christmas Eve drink
Dried fruits simmered in water until they release their sweetness
Sweetened with honey
Served cold or at room temperature
One of the 12 dishes of Sviata Vecheria (Christmas Eve dinner)
The 12 dishes represent the 12 apostles -- uzvar is the traditional drink among them
drinks.description: Ukrainian Christmas Eve dried fruit compote -- uzvar, dried apples, pears, prunes, and cherries simmered until sweet, finished with honey. Served cold. One of the 12 dishes of Sviata Vecheria (Christmas Eve). The 12 dishes represent the 12 apostles.
